title: How to Pass the Part 107 Exam: A 2026 Study Guide
sub_heading: ACS domains, realistic timelines, practice strategy, and test-day logistics—without guaranteed outcomes.
body_html:
Draft — review before import. Not legal or FAA official guidance.

In short: The FAA Part 107 knowledge test rewards steady coverage of ACS topics, repeated practice with exam-style questions, and honest scheduling—most prepared applicants need 2–8 weeks of focused study depending on background.

What the test covers (high level)

Topics span regulations, airspace, weather, loading and performance, and operations. Use the FAA ACS as the authoritative outline; prep courses should map units to those domains.

Study timeline

  • 2–3 weeks: aviation or manned pilot background
  • 4–6 weeks: typical career changer, 5–8 hrs/week
  • 8+ weeks: part-time or first exposure to airspace concepts

Practice strategy

Prefer structured unit quizzes over one massive cram session. Missed questions should drive review of the underlying section—not memorizing answer letters.

Test day

Schedule at an FAA-approved testing center; bring required ID; fee paid to testing center (not included in prep course prices).

How Drone Edge fits

Structured units, section practice, and course exams. Preview Unit 1 free before unlocking the full course.

Questions answered

Do you guarantee a pass?

No.

Is flight training included?

No—this is knowledge test preparation.
